name: Los Angeles
operatingHours: Metro rail runs ~4:30 AM–~midnight daily (~5:00 AM–~12:30 AM on some lines), with trains every 5–12 min by day and every 10–20 min late. There is no 24-hour rail service; some Metro buses run overnight.
fareInfo: Flat $1.75 per ride on any Metro bus or rail, with free transfers for 2 hours (2026). Tap a TAP card, TAP in a phone wallet, or a contactless bank card; fare capping stops charges at $5 per day and $18 per week. Airport shuttle from LAX to the K Line is free.

lines.name: Metro C Line
lines.firstLast: LAX/Metro Transit Center station: free LAX shuttle to the terminals; trains ~4:30 AM to ~midnight.

lines.name: Metro K Line
lines.firstLast: LAX/Metro Transit Center station: free LAX shuttle to the terminals; trains ~4:30 AM to ~midnight.

sights.name: Griffith Observatory
sights.note: Art-deco observatory on Mount Hollywood with free exhibits, telescopes and a close view of the Hollywood Sign and city.
sights.hours: 12:00–10:00 PM Tue–Fri, 10:00 AM–10:00 PM Sat–Sun, closed Mon

sights.name: Universal Studios Hollywood
sights.note: Film-studio theme park with a backlot tram tour and rides; reachable by Metro B Line to Universal City/Studio City and a short shuttle.
sights.hours: Hours vary by season, typically ~9:00 AM–6:00 PM or later

sights.name: The Getty Center
sights.note: Hilltop art museum with gardens and views, reached by a free tram from the parking base; admission is free.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:30 PM Tue–Fri & Sun, till 9:00 PM Sat, closed Mon

sights.name: Petersen Automotive Museum
sights.note: Four floors of rare and famous cars and motorcycles on Museum Row, in a striking steel-ribboned building.

sights.name: Venice Beach
sights.note: The wide beach and Ocean Front Walk boardwalk with street performers, Muscle Beach and skate park.

sights.name: California Science Center
sights.note: Free science museum in Exposition Park, home of the Space Shuttle Endeavour (timed passes) and large IMAX screen; confirm shuttle exhibit status before visiting.

sights.name: La Brea Tar Pits and Museum
sights.note: Active Ice Age fossil site beside LACMA, with a museum of mammoth and saber-tooth finds and bubbling asphalt pits.

sights.name: Hollywood Sign
sights.note: The famous hillside letters; best seen from Griffith Observatory or Lake Hollywood Park rather than up close.
sights.hours: Viewpoints open 24 hours; hiking access limited

sights.name: The Broad
sights.note: Free contemporary art museum with Kusama's Infinity Mirror Room, Koons and Warhol; downtown on Grand Avenue.
sights.hours: 11:00 AM–5:00 PM Tue–Fri, 10:00 AM–6:00 PM Sat–Sun, closed Mon

sights.name: Little Tokyo
sights.note: Historic Japanese-American district with ramen, mochi shops, the Japanese American National Museum and the Metro stop at its edge.
sights.hours: Streets open 24 hours; shops ~10:00 AM–9:00 PM

sights.name: The Original Farmers Market
sights.note: Since 1934, stalls of food counters and produce beside The Grove, a casual lunch stop.
sights.hours: Mon–Fri 9:00 AM–9:00 PM, Sat 9:00 AM–8:00 PM, Sun 10:00 AM–7:00 PM

sights.name: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
sights.note: The largest art museum in the western US, with Urban Light lamp-post installation at its entrance.
sights.hours: ~11:00 AM–5:00 PM Mon, Tue, Thu; till 8:00 PM Fri; 10:00 AM–7:00 PM Sat–Sun; closed Wed

sights.name: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County
sights.note: Dinosaurs, gems and a butterfly pavilion in a 1913 building in Exposition Park.

sights.name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
sights.note: Frank Gehry's stainless-steel concert hall; walk the garden and take a self-guided audio tour on non-rehearsal days.
sights.hours: Exterior and garden daily; tours vary with rehearsal schedule

sights.name: Grand Central Market
sights.note: 1917 downtown food hall with tacos, pupusas, coffee and the neon Eggslut line; a local-flavor lunch stop.

sights.name: Hollywood Walk of Fame
sights.note: Brass stars along Hollywood Boulevard, beside the TCL Chinese Theatre handprints; gritty but iconic.

sights.name: Union Station
sights.note: The 1939 Mission-revival and art-deco rail terminal with a grand waiting hall; also the city's transit hub.

railStations.name: Union Station
railStations.note: LA's rail hub: Amtrak Pacific Surfliner to San Diego/Santa Barbara, Coast Starlight and Southwest Chief long-distance trains, Metrolink commuter rail, and the FlyAway bus to LAX. Metro A, B and D lines stop in the station.
railStations.hours: Station open ~4:00 AM–midnight; trains run to individual timetables.

airports.name: Los Angeles International Airport
airports.transitNote: Not directly on the subway map: a free shuttle runs every ~10 min from the terminals to the LAX/Metro Transit Center (Aviation/Century on the C and K lines). From there the K Line to Expo/Crenshaw, then the E Line, reaches downtown 7th St/Metro Center in ~60–75 min total; $1.75. FlyAway bus to Union Station ~$10, ~45 min.
airports.hours: Metro rail first trains ~4:30–5:00 AM, last ~midnight; shuttle runs on a similar schedule.
